Title: PKCε is a negative regulator of PVAT-derived vessel formation.

--- ABSTRACT ---
[RATIONALE]: Vessel formation is a crucial event in tissue repair after injury. Thus, one assumption of innovative therapeutic approaches is the understanding of its molecular mechanisms. Notwithstanding our knowledge of the role of Protein Kinase C epsilon (PKCε) in cardio-protection and vascular restenosis, its role in vessel progenitor differentiation remains elusive.
[OBJECTIVE]: Given the availability of PKCε pharmacological modulators already tested in clinical trials, the specific aim of this study is to unravel the role of PKCε in vessel progenitor differentiation, with implications in vascular pathology and vasculogenesis.
[METHODS AND RESULTS]: Mouse Peri-Vascular Adipose Tissue (PVAT) was used as source of mesenchymal vessel progenitors. VEGF-induced differentiation of PVAT cells down-regulates both PKCε and p-PAK1 protein expression levels. PKCε overexpression and activation: i) reduced the expression levels of SMA and PECAM in endothelial differentiation of PVAT cells; ii) completely abrogated tubules formation in collagen gel assays; iii) increased the expression of p-PAK1.
[CONCLUSION]: PKCε negatively interferes with vessel progenitor differentiation via interaction with PAK-1.

Protein kinase C epsilon (PKCε) activation controls fibroblast growth factor-2 (FGF-2) angiogenic signaling. Here, we examined the effect of activating PKCε on FGF-2 dependent vascular growth and endothelial activation. ψεRACK, a selective PKCε agonist induces pro-angiogenic responses in endothelial cells, including formation of capillary like structures and cell growth. These effects are mediated by FGF-2 export to the cell membrane, as documented by biotinylation and immunofluorescence, and FGF-2/FGFR1 signaling activation, as attested by ERK1/2-STAT-3 phosphorylation and de novo FGF-2 synthesis. In vivo ψεRACK does not induce angiogenesis in the rabbit cornea. However, ψεRACK promotes VEGF angiogenic responses, an effect sustained by endothelial FGF-2 release and synthesis, since anti-FGF-2 antibody strongly attenuates VEGF responses. key_findings.finding: Direct evidence supports that PKCε/PRKCE is a negative regulator of PVAT-derived vessel formation in a mouse model: VEGF-induced differentiation of mouse PVAT mesenchymal vessel progenitors down-regulated PKCε and phospho-PAK1, whereas PKCε overexpression/activation reduced SMA and PECAM expression and completely abolished tubule formation in collagen-gel assays. The study concluded that PKCε interferes negatively with vessel-progenitor differentiation through PAK1 interaction. Evidence is from one direct experimental study (PMID 25433270), and the abstract does not establish an in-vivo PVAT neovascularization outcome.

source_tools.relevance: Direct PVAT experimental study and abstract evidence
Annotation corroborating mouse, PVAT-related vessel markers, and PRKCE/VEGFA relationship
Initial focused search identifying the exact direct study

key_findings.finding: Indirect angiogenesis evidence points in the opposite direction: in cultured coronary venular endothelial cells, selective PKCε activation with ψεRACK increased endothelial proliferation, migration, capillary-like structures, and sprouting; effects were reversed by a PKCε antagonist or PKCε siRNA. PKCε stimulation promoted FGF-2 release/FGFR1 signaling and enhanced VEGF angiogenic responses, although ψεRACK alone did not induce angiogenesis in the rabbit cornea. This is endothelial-cell angiogenesis evidence, not PVAT-derived vessel formation.

key_findings.finding: Overall conclusion: PKCε can be described as a negative regulator specifically of PVAT progenitor differentiation/tubule formation based on the direct mouse PVAT study, but not as a universal inhibitor of angiogenesis. In non-PVAT endothelial models, PKCε activation is pro-angiogenic or permissive for VEGF responses; therefore tissue/cell context and assay type are critical, and evidence for direct inhibition of mature-vessel neovascularization in vivo is insufficient.
